lem-ip-calderon-bourgain-cutoff-estimate:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $s\ge1$, and let $e_1,e_2\in\mathbb R^d$ be orthonormal. Put $\zeta=s(e_1-ie_2)$ and
$$p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi.$$
Use the unitary angular-frequency Fourier transform $\widehat u(\xi)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}u(x)\,dx$, and set
$$\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^b}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|p_\zeta(\xi)|^{2b}|\widehat u(\xi)|^2\,d\xi,\qquad \|u\|_{X_\zeta^b}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^d}(s+|p_\zeta(\xi)|)^{2b}|\widehat u(\xi)|^2\,d\xi.$$
For every fixed Schwartz function $\phi$, a constant $C=C(d,\phi)$ independent of $s,e_1,e_2$ satisfies, for all Schwartz $u$,
$$\|\phi u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}\le C\|u\|_{X_\zeta^{-1/2}},\qquad \|\phi u\|_{X_\zeta^{1/2}}\le C\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}.$$
Consequently
$$\|\phi u\|_2\le Cs^{-1/2}\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}},\qquad \|\nabla(\phi u)\|_2\le Cs^{1/2}\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}.$$
The norms are finite on Schwartz space; the values of the weights on the measure-zero characteristic sphere do not affect them. All four maps extend continuously to the completions in the respective input norms.
lem-ip-planar-cauchy-beurling-and-near-t:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$, use angular-frequency unitary Fourier transformation, and put $\partial=(\partial_x-i\partial_y)/2$, $\bar\partial=(\partial_x+i\partial_y)/2$. The Beurling transform $\mathcal B$ defined on $L^2(\mathbb C)$ by
$$\widehat{\mathcal Bf}(\xi)=\frac{\xi_1-i\xi_2}{\xi_1+i\xi_2}\widehat f(\xi)\qquad(\xi\ne0)$$
is an isometry and extends boundedly to every $L^p$, $1<p<\infty$. It commutes with translations. There is a finite constant $A\ge1$ such that, for $2\le p\le4$,
$$\|\mathcal B\|_{L^p\to L^p}\le A^{2-4/p}.$$
For $p>2$ and $f\in L^p$ supported in a fixed disk $D_R$, the absolutely convergent integral
$$\mathcal Cf(z):=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb C}\frac{f(w)}{z-w}\,dA(w)$$
belongs to $W^{1,p}(\mathbb C)$, satisfies $\bar\partial\mathcal Cf=f$, $\partial\mathcal Cf=\mathcal Bf$, and obeys
$$\|\mathcal Cf\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C_{p,R}\|f\|_p,\qquad |\mathcal Cf(z)-\mathcal Cf(z')|\le C_p\|f\|_p|z-z'|^{1-2/p}.$$
It is $O(1/|z|)$ at infinity. For every $0\le\kappa<1$ there is $p_\kappa>2$ such that, whenever $2\le p\le p_\kappa$ and $\mu,\nu$ are measurable with $\||\mu|+|\nu|\|_\infty\le\kappa$, the real-linear map
$$I-\mu\mathcal B-\nu\overline{\mathcal B},\qquad \overline{\mathcal B}(f):=\overline{\mathcal Bf},$$
is invertible on $L^p(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$, with inverse norm at most $2/(1-\kappa)$.
lem-ip-calderon-averaged-negative-bourga:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $k\in\mathbb R^d$, and fix an oriented two-plane $P\perp k$. For a unit vector $\eta\in P$, let $\eta^\perp$ be its positive quarter turn. For $s\ge|k|/2$, put $r(s)=\sqrt{s^2-|k|^2/4}$ and
$$\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)=\pm s\eta+i(k/2\pm r(s)\eta^\perp).$$
These phases are null, have length $\sqrt2s$, and sum to $ik$. Use the unitary angular Fourier convention and the norms $\dot X_\zeta^b,X_\zeta^b$ with inhomogeneous weight $s+|p_\zeta|$, where $p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi$. For a fixed $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, define
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f):=\frac1\lambda\int_{S^1(P)}\int_\lambda^{2\lambda}\|\phi\operatorname{div}f\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)}^{-1/2}}^2\,ds\,d\eta.$$
Here $d\eta$ is arclength, either sign can be used, and the derivative is distributional. For $\lambda\ge100\sqrt{1+|k|^2}$ and $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C^d)$,
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le C\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\|f\|_2^2,$$
where $C$ depends only on $d,\phi$. If $f\in H^1$, also
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le\frac C\lambda\|\nabla f\|_2^2.$$
Let $\rho\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))$ be nonnegative with integral $1$, put $\rho_h(x)=h^{-d}\rho(x/h)$, and define $\omega_2(f,h)=\sup_{|y|\le h}\|f(\cdot-y)-f\|_2$. For $h>0$ one consequently has
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le C_\rho\left[\frac{\|f\|_2^2}{\lambda h^2}+\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\omega_2(f,h)^2\right].$$
lem-ip-planar-beltrami-caccioppoli-trans:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<j\}$, let $0\le\kappa<1$, and let $2<r\le p_\kappa$, where $p_\kappa$ is a near-two inverse exponent. Put $q=2r/(r-2)$, so $1/2=1/q+1/r$. Let $\mu,\nu$ be measurable, supported in $D_3$, and satisfy $\||\mu|+|\nu|\|_\infty\le\kappa$. Suppose $f\in W^{1,r}(D_3;\mathbb C)$ satisfies
$$\bar\partial f=\mu\partial f+\nu\overline{\partial f}$$
almost everywhere. Fix a real $\phi\in C_c^\infty(D_2)$ and extend $F=\phi f$ by zero. Then
$$\|\bar\partial F\|_r+\|\partial F\|_r\le C_{\kappa,r}\|f\nabla\phi\|_r.$$
For $\omega_p(g,t):=\sup_{|h|\le t}\|g(\cdot-h)-g\|_p$, $G=\bar\partial F$, and $U=\|f\|_{W^{1,r}(D_3)}$, one has, when $0<t\le1/2$,
$$\omega_2(G,t)+\omega_2(\phi\bar\partial f,t)\le C_{\kappa,r,\phi}U\bigl(\omega_q(\mu,t)+\omega_q(\nu,t)+t\bigr).$$
For the unitary angular Fourier transform and $T\ge6$, this implies
$$\|\mathbf1_{\{|\xi|\ge T\}}\widehat G\|_2\le C_{\kappa,r,\phi}U\bigl(\omega_q(\mu,3/T)+\omega_q(\nu,3/T)+T^{-1}\bigr).$$
lem-ip-planar-principal-beltrami-inverse:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$ and $R,S>0$. For every measurable $\mu$ supported in $D_R=\{|z|<R\}$ with $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$, there is a unique quasiconformal homeomorphism $\Phi:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ satisfying
$$\bar\partial\Phi=\mu\partial\Phi,\qquad \Phi(z)=z+O(1/z)\quad(z\to\infty).$$
Choose any fixed $2<r\le p_\kappa$ from the near-two inversion result, and put $\sigma=r-2>0$. Uniformly over all these coefficients,
$$\|\Phi-z\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}+\|\Phi-z\|_\infty+[\Phi-z]_{C^{0,1-2/r}}\le C_{\kappa,r,R},\qquad \int_{D_S}|\partial\Phi|^{-\sigma}\,dA\le C_{\kappa,r,R,S}.$$
The Jacobian and $\partial\Phi$ are positive and nonzero almost everywhere, respectively, so the negative power is well-defined almost everywhere. In particular, for any $|k|=1$ and $f(z)=e^{ik\Phi(z)}$,
$$\|f\|_{W^{1,r}(D_S)}+\bigl\||\partial f|^{-1}\bigr\|_{L^\sigma(D_S)}\le C_{\kappa,r,R,S}.$$
For $0<\sigma<1$ the displayed $L^\sigma$ quantity means $(\int|\partial f|^{-\sigma})^{1/\sigma}$, without asserting a norm triangle inequality.
lem-ip-planar-scattering-topological-zer:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $B,C>0$ and $0<b<1$. Let $g\in C^1(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$, let $\ell\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, and suppose $g(0)=0$ and
$$|g(k)-\ell k|\le C|k|^{1-b}\qquad(|k|\ge1).$$
Suppose distributionally $\bar\partial g=\sigma g+E$, where $\sigma$ is measurable, $\|\sigma\|_\infty\le B$, $E\in C^1$, and for $0<\delta\le1/2$,
$$|E(k)|\le C\delta e^{C|k|},\qquad |\nabla E(k)|\le C e^{C(1+|k|)}.$$
There exist $D>0$ and $\delta_0\in(0,1/2)$, depending only on $B,C,b$, such that
$$|\ell|\ge D[\log(1/\delta)]^{-b},\quad0<\delta<\delta_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g(k)\ne0\text{ for every }k\ne0.$$
If $E=0$, the same conclusion holds for every $\ell\ne0$, without a threshold condition.
def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.
lem-ip-calderon-disk-inclusion-perimeter:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $x_0\in\mathbb R^2$, $r>0$, $E=B(x_0,r)$, and let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be open with $\overline E\subset D$. Then $\chi_E\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$, its distributional derivative is
$$D\chi_E=-\nu_E\,\mathcal H^1|_{\partial E},\qquad \nu_E(x)=\frac{x-x_0}{r},$$
and
$$TV(\chi_E;\mathbb R^2)=TV(\chi_E;D)=2\pi r.$$
lem-ip-calderon-rough-potential-cgo-cons:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge3$, $0<\alpha<1$, a ball $B\subset\mathbb R^d$, and $K>0$. Let $\gamma\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)$ be real and positive, equal to $1$ outside $B$, and put $a=\nabla\log\gamma$. Suppose
$$\|a\|_\infty+[a]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)}\le K.$$
Define the compactly supported distribution $q$ and its multiplication form by
$$\langle q,v\rangle=-\frac12\int a\cdot\nabla v+\frac14\int |a|^2v,\qquad \langle m_q u,v\rangle=-\frac12\int a\cdot\nabla(uv)+\frac14\int |a|^2uv.$$
These pairings are complex bilinear. For the angular Fourier norms with $p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi$, there are constants $C,s_0\ge1$, depending only on $d,\alpha,B,K$, such that for every null phase $\zeta$ of length $\sqrt2s$ with $s\ge s_0$,
$$\|m_q\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}\to\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}\le Cs^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}\le\frac12.$$
There is $r_\zeta\in\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}\cap H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$U_\zeta(x)=e^{x\cdot\zeta}(1+r_\zeta(x)),\qquad (-\Delta+q)U_\zeta=0,\qquad \|r_\zeta\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}\le2\|q\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}.$$
The equation uses the multiplication form above against compactly supported smooth tests. For the phases $\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)$ associated to $k$ and $P\perp k$, if $\lambda\ge\max\{s_0,100\sqrt{1+|k|^2}\}$, then for either sign,
$$\frac1\lambda\int_{S^1(P)}\int_\lambda^{2\lambda}\left(\|q\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm}^{-1/2}}^2+\|r_{\zeta_\pm}\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm}^{1/2}}^2\right)ds\,d\eta\le C\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\lambda^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}.$$
lem-ip-planar-conductivity-l2-interpolat:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $0\le\kappa<1$, $2<r\le p_\kappa$, $q=2r/(r-2)$, $0<\theta\le1$, and $A,U,V>0$. For $j=1,2$, let $\mu_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb R)$ be supported in $D_1$, with $\|\mu_j\|_\infty\le\kappa$ and
$$\omega_q(\mu_j,t)\le At^\theta\qquad(0<t\le1/2).$$
Let $f_j\in W^{1,r}(D_3;\mathbb C)$ satisfy $\bar\partial f_j=\mu_j\overline{\partial f_j}$ and $\|f_j\|_{W^{1,r}(D_3)}\le U$. Suppose, for some $\sigma>0$,
$$\int_{D_1}|\partial f_2|^{-\sigma}\,dA\le V^\sigma.$$
Then there is $C=C(\kappa,r,\theta,A,U,V,\sigma)$ such that, if $\varepsilon=\|f_1-f_2\|_{L^\infty(D_2)}\le1$,
$$\|\mu_1-\mu_2\|_{L^2(D_1)}\le C\varepsilon^\eta,\qquad \eta=\frac{\theta\sigma}{(1+\theta)(2+\sigma)}>0.$$
The same estimate holds for $\gamma_j=(1-\mu_j)/(1+\mu_j)$ after increasing $C$. In particular, a logarithmic bound $\varepsilon\le C_0[\log(1/\delta)]^{-b}$ with $b>0$ gives an $L^2$ conductivity bound with exponent $b\eta$, and $\varepsilon=0$ gives equality of the conductivities.
lem-ip-planar-measurable-beltrami-cgo-so:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$ and $2<r\le p_\kappa$ from the near-two inverse. Let $\mu\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$ be supported in $D_1$, with $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$. For each $k\in\mathbb C$ there is a unique solution
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ikz}M_\mu(z,k),\qquad M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C),\qquad M_\mu(z,k)=1+O(1/z)$$
of $\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu\overline{\partial f_\mu}$, with $f_\mu(\cdot,0)=1$. The function $M_\mu$ never vanishes and
$$\|M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}\le C_{\kappa,r} |k|e^{C_{\kappa,r}|k|}.$$
When $k\ne0$, it has a representation
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ik\Phi_\mu(z,k)},$$
where $\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)$ is a principal $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism, $K=(1+\kappa)/(1-\kappa)$, conformal outside $\overline D_1$, and
$$\|\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)-z\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}+\sup_z(1+|z|)|\Phi_\mu(z,k)-z|\le C_{\kappa,r}.$$
Consequently $\|f_\mu(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}(D_S)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}|k|}$; for $|k|=1$, the inverse-gradient bound $\int_{D_S}|\partial f_\mu|^{-(r-2)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}$ also holds uniformly.
lem-ip-planar-qc-composition-preserves-p:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$, $2<r\le p_\kappa$, $q\ge1$, and $L,R,A,B>0$. Put $p=qr/(r-2)$ and $\theta_0=1-2/r$. Let $\Phi$ be a principal quasiconformal homeomorphism with coefficient supported in $D_L$ and bounded by $\kappa$, and let $\Psi=\Phi^{-1}$. Suppose $v$ is measurable, supported in $D_R$, with $\|v\|_\infty\le B$ and
$$\omega_p(v,t):=\sup_{|h|\le t}\|v(\cdot-h)-v\|_p\le At^\theta\qquad(0<t\le1),$$
where $0<\theta\le1$. Then $v\circ\Psi$ is a well-defined almost-everywhere class, is supported in a fixed disk depending only on the listed parameters, and
$$\omega_q(v\circ\Psi,t)\le C t^{\theta\theta_0/(1+\theta)}\qquad(0<t\le1).$$
The constant is uniform over all such $v,\Phi$. Thus the positive power translation moduli furnished by bounded BV conductivities remain positive power moduli after these changes of variables.
lem-ip-planar-oscillatory-beltrami-phase:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0<\kappa<1$, $R,A>0$, $q>2$ and $0<\theta\le1$. Let $\mu$ be measurable, supported in $D_R$, with $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$ and $\omega_q(\mu,t)\le At^\theta$ for $0<t\le1$. For $v\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$ and $|c_v|=1$, let $\Psi_v$ be the principal quasiconformal solution of
$$\bar\partial\Psi_v(z)=c_v e^{iv\cdot z}\mu(z)\partial\Psi_v(z).$$
There exist $C>0$ and $b>0$, depending only on $\kappa,R,A,q,\theta$, such that
$$\sup_{z\in\mathbb C}|\Psi_v(z)-z|\le C|v|^{-b}\qquad(|v|\ge1).$$
Both constants are uniform in $\mu$, the direction of $v$ and its unimodular factor $c_v$.
def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.
lem-ip-calderon-fixed-collar-c1alpha-ext:
## Statement

Let $d\ge3$ and let $\gamma\in X_d(R)$ for the domain, collar, ellipticity bounds and exponent $0<\alpha<1$ defining that class. Extend $\gamma$ by $1$ outside $\Omega$, using its continuous representative on $\overline\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)$, $\gamma_e-1$ has support contained in $\overline{\Omega'}$, and
$$\min\{m,1\}\le\gamma_e\le M,\qquad \sup_{\mathbb R^d}|\gamma_e|\le\max\{R,1\},\qquad \sup_{\mathbb R^d}|\partial_j\gamma_e|\le R,\qquad [\partial_j\gamma_e]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)}\le R.$$
Here the Hölder seminorm is $[f]_{C^{0,\alpha}}:=\sup_{x\ne y}|f(x)-f(y)|/|x-y|^\alpha$, and $j=1,\ldots,d$.
lem-ip-planar-beltrami-cgo-power-phase-d:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0<\kappa<1$, choose $2<r\le p_\kappa$, and put $p=4r/(r-2)$. Suppose $\mu\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$ is supported in $D_1$, $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$, and $\omega_p(\mu,t)\le At^\theta$ for $0<t\le1$, with fixed $A>0$ and $0<\theta\le1$. Let $f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ik\Phi_\mu(z,k)}$ be its measurable-coefficient Beltrami CGO solution and principal phase. There exist constants $C,b>0$, depending only on $\kappa,r,A,\theta$, such that
$$|\Phi_\mu(z,k)-z|\le C\min\{(1+|z|)^{-1},|k|^{-b}\}\qquad(z\in\mathbb C,\ |k|\ge1).$$
The same constants apply to every coefficient $\lambda\mu$, $|\lambda|=1$.
lem-ip-planar-forced-beltrami-similarity:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$ and $2<r\le p_\kappa$. Let $\nu,\alpha,E$ be measurable and supported in $D_1$, with $\|\nu\|_\infty\le\kappa$, $\|\alpha\|_\infty\le B$ and $E\in L^r$. If $F\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ is continuous, tends to zero at infinity, and satisfies
$$\bar\partial F=\nu\overline{\partial F}+\alpha\overline F+E,$$
then
$$\|F\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}+\|F\|_\infty\le C_{\kappa,r}e^{C_{\kappa,r}(1+B)}\|E\|_r.$$
The constants do not depend on the measurable coefficients or on the particular solution.
lem-ip-calderon-rough-dn-map-wellposedne:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.
lem-ip-planar-conductivity-cgo-logarithm:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$ and bounded by $0<\kappa<1$, and put $\gamma=(1-\mu)/(1+\mu)$. Let $f_\pm=f_{\pm\mu}$ be the measurable Beltrami CGO solutions. Then
$$\operatorname{Re}\frac{f_+(z,k)}{f_-(z,k)}>0,\qquad u_\gamma(z,k):=\operatorname{Re}f_+(z,k)+i\operatorname{Im}f_-(z,k)\ne0.$$
The function $u_\gamma$ solves $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u_\gamma)=0$ weakly, has the form $e^{ikz}(1+R_\gamma)$ with $R_\gamma\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and $R_\gamma(z,k)=O(1/z)$, and $u_\gamma(\cdot,0)=1$. For $k\ne0$ there is a continuous logarithmic phase $\delta_\gamma(\cdot,k)$, uniquely normalized by
$$u_\gamma(z,k)=e^{\delta_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz=O(1/z)\quad(z\to\infty).$$
It maps $\mathbb C$ onto $\mathbb C$. If the power-modulus hypotheses of the Beltrami phase-decay result hold, uniformly for unimodular multiples of $\mu$, then for some $C,b>0$,
$$|\delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz|\le C|k|\min\{(1+|z|)^{-1},|k|^{-b}\}\qquad(|k|\ge1).$$
For each fixed $k$, $u_\gamma$ is uniformly Hölder continuous on every fixed disk, with an exponent $1-2/r>0$ and a constant depending only on that disk, $\kappa,r,|k|$.
lem-ip-bv-translation-modulus-for-conduc:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and let $d=2$ with the conductivity class $X_2(R)$ of the Calderón admissible class. For $\gamma\in X_2(R)$ let $\widetilde{\gamma-1}$ be the zero extension of $\gamma-1$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb R^2$ and set $\gamma_e:=1+\widetilde{\gamma-1}$. Define $B:=\max\{1,M,m^{-1}\}$. There is a constant $C_1$ depending only on $\Omega,m,M,R$ such that
$$\|\gamma_e(\cdot+h)-\gamma_e\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_1|h|\qquad(h\in\mathbb R^2).$$
For every finite $p>2B$ there is $C_p<\infty$, depending only on $\Omega,m,M,R,p$, such that
$$\sup_{\gamma\in X_2(R)}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}\|\gamma_e(\cdot+h)-\gamma_e\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_p t^{1/p}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
The extension is an almost-everywhere measurable class; no pointwise continuity is asserted.
lem-ip-calderon-radial-inclusion-dn-spec:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $D=B(x_0,a)\subset(0,1)^2$ be a disk with $a>0$, let $0<r\le a/2$, and let $\beta>0$. Define $\gamma_1\equiv1$ on $D$ and $\gamma_r:=1+\beta\chi_{B(x_0,r)}$, and put $\eta:=\beta/(2+\beta)$. Both conductivities belong to $\Gamma_{1,1+\beta}(D)$. For each $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, with $n:=|k|$ and boundary Fourier mode $e_k(\theta):=e^{ik\theta}$, the induced weak DN maps on the trace quotient by constants satisfy
$$\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}e_k,\qquad \dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta(r/a)^{2n}}{1-\eta(r/a)^{2n}}e_k,$$
under the $L^2(\partial D)$ dual pairing; both maps annihilate the constant boundary class. If $Q_n:=\|[e_k]\|_{\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1}^2$ is the squared trace-quotient-by-constants norm of the mode, then
$$2\pi n\le Q_n\le 2\pi n+\frac{\pi a^2}{n+1},$$
and
$$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}(r/a)^2.$$
lem-ip-calderon-rough-alessandrini-and-q:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ be real measurable conductivities with $0<m\le\gamma_j\le M<\infty$ almost everywhere. Put $\mathcal D=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ and $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$, both with their quotient norms. For $f_j\in\mathcal D$, let $u_j$ be the weak $\gamma_j$-conductivity solution with trace class $f_j$. Then
$$((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1)(f_2)=\int_\Omega(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\nabla u_1\cdot\overline{\nabla u_2}\,dx.$$
The exact norm equality
$$\|\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D,\mathcal D^*)}=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)}=:\delta$$
holds, and consequently the integral above has absolute value at most $\delta\|[f_1]\|_E\|[f_2]\|_E$, and at most $\delta\|u_1\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. Here $[f_j]$ denotes the coset modulo constants; the stars denote continuous conjugate-linear duals.
lem-ip-planar-scattering-dbar-equation-a:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$, and $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa<1$. Fix $2<r\le p_\kappa$. Write $f_\pm=e^{ikz}M_\pm$, let $b_\pm(k)$ be the coefficients of $z^{-1}$ in the holomorphic exterior expansions $M_\pm(z,k)=1+b_\pm(k)/z+O(z^{-2})$, and define
$$\tau_\mu(k):=\tfrac12\overline{b_+(k)-b_-(k)}.$$
The functions $k\mapsto M_\pm(\cdot,k)-1$ are smooth into $W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and
$$\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}}+\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_\infty+|\nabla_k\tau_\mu(k)|\le C_{\kappa,r}e^{C_{\kappa,r}(1+|k|)}.$$
The amplitude obeys $\tau_\mu(0)=0$ and $|\tau_\mu(k)|\le1$. The conductivity CGO solution and its normalized logarithmic phase satisfy
$$\bar\partial_k u_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)\overline{u_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \bar\partial_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)e^{\overline{\delta_\gamma(z,k)}-\delta_\gamma(z,k)}.$$
For every fixed $S>0$, $|\nabla_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)|\le C_{\kappa,r,S}e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)}$ on $D_S$. The phase is normalized by $\delta_\gamma(z,0)=0$.
lem-ip-calderon-higher-dimensional-cgo-f:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $0<\alpha<1$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, and fix $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$ and $R>0$. For every $\gamma,\gamma_0\in X_d(R)$ there exist constants $C>0$, $\rho>0$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $d,\alpha,\Omega,\Omega',m,M,R$, such that
$$\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\omega\!\left(\|\dot{\Lambda}_\gamma-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_0}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\right),$$
where $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the trace quotient and $\dot\Lambda_\gamma$ is the induced weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on the constant quotient, and
$$\omega(0):=0,\qquad \omega(t):=\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{t,t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(t>0).$$
lem-ip-planar-dn-to-scattering-lipschitz:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $0<a<1$, $0\le\kappa<1$, and let real $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be supported in $D_a$, with $\|\mu_j\|_\infty\le\kappa$. Set $\gamma_j=(1-\mu_j)/(1+\mu_j)$, and define their weak DN maps on $D_1$ and their scattering amplitudes $\tau_j$ by the preceding CGO construction. If $E=\mathcal D(D_1)/\mathbb C\mathbf1$ and
$$\delta=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)},$$
then
$$|\tau_1(k)-\tau_2(k)|\le C_\kappa\delta |k|e^{C_\kappa(1+|k|)}\qquad(k\in\mathbb C).$$
In particular this is at most $C_\kappa\delta e^{C_\kappa(1+|k|)}$ after increasing the constant; the assertion includes $k=0$.
lem-ip-planar-dn-enclosure-and-reciproca:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^2$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain and let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$. Let $\gamma_j$ be real conductivities, $m\le\gamma_j\le M$ almost everywhere, equal to $1$ outside $\Omega'$, with $0<m\le M$. Extend them by $1$ to the disk $B=(1/2,1/2)+D_1$. On each domain use the weak energy DN map with trace space $\mathcal D=H^1/H_0^1$ and quotient $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$. Denote the constant-quotient DN difference norms by $\delta_\Omega(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ and $\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$. Then
$$\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\le C\delta_\Omega(\gamma_1,\gamma_2),\qquad \delta_B(\gamma_1^{-1},\gamma_2^{-1})\le C\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2),$$
where $C$ depends only on $m,M$ and the fixed geometry. Translation of $B$ to $D_1$ preserves these norms. In particular both disk data differences are bounded by a constant times the original measurement error, and both Beltrami coefficients have support in $D_a$ after this translation for a fixed $a<1$.
lem-ip-calderon-planar-beltrami-dbar-log:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^2$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, and fix $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$ and $R>0$. For every $\gamma,\gamma_0\in X_2(R)$ there exist constants $C>0$, $\rho>0$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $\Omega,\Omega',m,M,R$, such that
$$\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\omega\!\left(\|\dot{\Lambda}_\gamma-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_0}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\right),$$
where $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the trace quotient and $\dot\Lambda_\gamma$ is the induced weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on the constant quotient, and
$$\omega(0):=0,\qquad \omega(t):=\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{t,t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(t>0).$$
thm-ip-calderon-logarithmic-l2-stability:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For each fixed integer $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, fix $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$, and let $\gamma,\gamma_0\in X_d(R)$. Set
$$\delta:=\|\dot{\Lambda}_\gamma-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_0}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}.$$
There exist constants $C>0$, $\rho>0$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $d,\alpha,\Omega,\Omega',m,M,R$, such that
$$\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\omega(\delta),\qquad \omega(0):=0,\qquad \omega(t):=\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{t,t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(t>0).$$
Here $X_d(R)$ is the BV class when $d=2$ and the bounded $C^{1,\alpha}$ class when $d\ge3$, and $\dot\Lambda_\gamma$ is the induced weak conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on the trace quotient by constants.
